title: Constant polynomial resolution, differential retraction and evaluation augmentation
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $E$ any set, $P=A[x_e\mid e\in E]$, and $Q_\bullet$ the constant simplicial $A$-algebra on $P$, with identity faces, degeneracies and augmentation to $P$. Use the standard resolution $R_\bullet=P^{\mathrm{std}}_\bullet(P/A)$, its evaluation augmentation $\epsilon$, and the nonpositive alternating-face convention of [def-trf-cotangent-resolution-data]. Then $Q_\bullet\to P$ is a polynomial resolution: its terms are polynomial and surject onto $P$, and $s(Q_\bullet)\to P[0]$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Put $M=\Omega^1_{P/A}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] and $K=s(\Omega^1_{Q_\bullet/A}\otimes_{Q_\bullet}P)$. The multiplication identifications $\Omega^1_{Q_n/A}\otimes_{Q_n}P\cong M$, $\mathrm dq\otimes p\mapsto p\,\mathrm dq$, identify $K$ with the alternating-face complex of the constant simplicial $P$-module $M$, including all simplicial operators. In these coordinates $K^{-n}=M$ for $n\geq0$, its positive terms vanish, and $d^{-n}:K^{-n}\to K^{-n+1}$ is zero for odd $n$ and the identity for positive even $n$. Let $a:K\to M[0]$ and $j:M[0]\to K$ be identity in degree zero and zero in all other degrees. The maps $h^{-n}:K^{-n}\to K^{-n-1}$ equal to the identity for positive odd $n$ and zero for even $n\geq0$, with all positive-degree components zero, satisfy $aj=1$ and $dh+hd=1-ja$. Thus $a$ is a chain homotopy equivalence. The augmented evaluation map $R_\bullet\to Q_\bullet$ induces the chain map $v:s(\Omega^1_{R_\bullet/A}\otimes_{R_\bullet}P)\to K$ whose degree $-n$ formula is $\mathrm dq\otimes p\mapsto p\,\mathrm d(\epsilon_n(q))$. The composite $av$ is precisely the canonical differential augmentation of the standard cotangent complex: its degree-zero formula is $\mathrm dq\otimes p\mapsto p\,\mathrm d(\epsilon_0(q))$, and its other components vanish.

source.place: Tags 08QG (lemma-pi-lower-shriek-polynomial-algebra), 08QH (lemma-cotangent-complex-polynomial-algebra), 08QI (remark-resolution), and 08QL (section-functoriality): explicit constant-resolution contraction and evaluation formulas from returned proof Steps 1--2.

proof.text: Every term of $Q_\bullet$ is $P=A[x_e\mid e\in E]$ and its augmentation is the identity, hence is surjective. All faces are identities, so for $n>0$ its alternating differential is $(\sum_{i=0}^n(-1)^i)1_P$: zero for odd $n$, identity for even $n$, by cancelling successive pairs. Thus $H^0(s(Q))=P/0=P$. For odd $n>0$, $H^{-n}=P/P=0$, since the incoming differential is the identity; for even $n>0$, $H^{-n}=0/0=0$, since the outgoing differential is the identity. Positive terms vanish. The augmentation induces the identity in degree-zero cohomology and the unique isomorphisms between zero groups otherwise. This is precisely a polynomial resolution under the cited definition.

source.place: Tags 08QG (lemma-pi-lower-shriek-polynomial-algebra), 08QI (remark-resolution): direct alternating-complex check of the constant resolution.

proof.text: Because $Q_n=P$ with identity augmentation, put $\mu_n:\Omega^1_{Q_n/A}\otimes_{Q_n}P\to M$, $\omega\otimes p\mapsto p\omega$. This is balanced: $\mu_n(q\omega\otimes p)=pq\omega=\mu_n(\omega\otimes qp)$. Its inverse is $\omega\mapsto\omega\otimes1$, since $p\omega\otimes1=\omega\otimes p$. Universal differentials are generated by $\mathrm dq$, by their quotient presentation in the cited definition. Every simplicial operator of $Q$ is the identity on $P$, so its differential operator sends $\mathrm dq\otimes p$ to the same tensor. The identifications $\mu_n$ therefore intertwine every face and degeneracy with $1_M$. (The convention $p\otimes\mathrm dq$ in the resolution-data node is equivalent by the tensor flip over the commutative ring.) Consequently $K^{-n}=M$, its positive terms vanish, and the same alternating-sum calculation as in Step 1 gives exactly the claimed differential.

source.place: Tags 08QH (lemma-cotangent-complex-polynomial-algebra), 08QI (remark-resolution): constant differential model, with tensor-unit identification written explicitly.

proof.text: The specified $a$ and $j$ commute with differentials: the only possibly nonzero boundary into degree zero is $d^{-1}=0$, and the differential out of degree zero has zero target. Clearly $aj=1$. Write $d_n=d^{-n}$ for $n>0$, $d_0=0$, and $h_n=h^{-n}$, with $h_{-1}=0$. In degree $-n$ the homotopy expression is $d_{n+1}h_n+h_{n-1}d_n$. For odd $n>0$ its first summand is $1_M$ and its second is zero; for even $n>0$ its first summand is zero and its second is $1_M$. For $n=0$ both vanish, as does $1-ja$; all positive-degree objects are zero. This proves $dh+hd=1-ja$ in every degree, so $j$ is a chain homotopy inverse of $a$. In particular, on cycles the difference $z-ja(z)=d(h(z))$ is a boundary, exhibiting the induced inverse maps on cohomology without invoking a homotopy-invariance theorem.

source.place: Tags 08QH (lemma-cotangent-complex-polynomial-algebra), 08QI (remark-resolution): explicit parity contraction of the constant differential complex.

proof.text: The standard evaluation augmentation is an augmented simplicial $A$-algebra map $\epsilon:R_\bullet\to Q_\bullet$, since $Q$ is constant on its target $P$. For each $n$, the map $q\mapsto\mathrm d(\epsilon_n(q))$ is an $A$-derivation into $M$ viewed as an $R_n$-module via $\epsilon_n$: the Leibniz formula is $\mathrm d(\epsilon_n(qq'))=\epsilon_n(q)\mathrm d(\epsilon_n(q'))+\epsilon_n(q')\mathrm d(\epsilon_n(q))$. Universality yields the corresponding $R_n$-linear map on $\Omega^1_{R_n/A}$, and balancing extends it to the $P$-linear map $v^{-n}(\mathrm dq\otimes p)=p\,\mathrm d(\epsilon_n(q))$. Explicitly the balancing relation is respected because both $(r\,\mathrm dq)\otimes p$ and $\mathrm dq\otimes\epsilon_n(r)p$ map to $p\epsilon_n(r)\mathrm d(\epsilon_n(q))$. For any simplicial operator $\theta:R_n\to R_m$, augmentation compatibility says $\epsilon_m\theta=\epsilon_n$. Applying both composites to $\mathrm dq\otimes p$ gives $p\,\mathrm d(\epsilon_n(q))$. The maps therefore commute with every simplicial operator, hence with their alternating sums. This constructs the induced chain map $v$ with the asserted formula in the coordinates of Step 2.

source.place: Tags 08QL (section-functoriality), 08QI (remark-resolution): differential map of the evaluation augmentation; universal-derivation construction.

proof.text: Composition with $a$ leaves the degree-zero formula of $v$ unchanged and kills every other degree. This degree-zero map annihilates the incoming boundary: on a generator in degree $-1$ its value on the alternating boundary is $p\,\mathrm d(\epsilon_0(d_0q))-p\,\mathrm d(\epsilon_0(d_1q))=0$, because both augmented faces equal $\epsilon_1(q)$. Thus these components are exactly the differential augmentation from the standard complex to $M[0]$. They uniquely determine it: degree zero is generated by the tensors $\mathrm dq\otimes p$, and all other target terms are zero. Accordingly $av$ is the canonical augmentation, with the claimed evaluation formula, rather than merely some map with isomorphic target.

source.place: Tags 08PN (definition-cotangent-complex-ring-map), 08QL (section-functoriality): evaluation description of the differential augmentation.
